discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling in a time-reversal-invariant insulator can produce a quantum spin Hall phase, classified by a new Z2 topological invariant and carrying helical edge states protected by symmetry. Molenkamp's group gave the decisive experimental confirmation in 2007, observing quantized edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells, and later demonstrated the nonlocal helical transport. This work established that symmetry and topology together define new electronic phases in ordinary materials. It led directly to three-dimensional topological insulators, to the periodic table of topological phases, and to the program of topological superconductivity and Majorana bound states at superconductor/topological insulator interfaces, which Kane himself initiated with Fu. Few ideas in condensed matter physics of the past two decades have combined such conceptual clarity, sharp testable predictions for transport experiments, and lasting influence across fields.
